reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 32. Nay or No: 6. Not Voting: 2. Of 38 Yea or Nay votes where the Republican majority could be computed, 37 (97%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 211 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: House roll calls 1–323 of 2026 (323 votes, January 6, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the House Clerk.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.
stands_for.factual_flag: Not yet summarized: this line is built only from the official vote question and the bill's official title.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

🚨We have officially subpoenaed the state of New Jersey over 6,600 noncitizens improperly registered to vote in New Jersey.

We’ve had enough of the stonewalling. 

The people of New Jersey deserve secure elections. https://t.co/QNJJnOLkIv

An illegal immigrant with an ICE detainer got drunk, got in a car, and put a NJ police officer in the hospital fighting to recover.

Sanctuary policies failed him.

Every politician who defends them owns this.
https://t.co/rmL1hrT7tn
Happy Columbus Day!🇺🇸 https://t.co/Tlq4WNEirp

The Coast Guard just recruited its largest class in nearly 40 years.

This is exactly why I fought to secure $425 million to modernize Training Center Cape May.

More Americans are stepping up to serve, and we are making sure South Jersey is ready to train them.

I am proud to secure $500,000 for the John R. Elliott HERO Campaign to help prevent drunk driving.

This funding will expand its designated driver message on police cruisers across the country.

If one of those cars makes someone think twice before driving drunk, that is a life https://t.co/OkoDCxnIH3

The nor’easter is hitting South Jersey right now with some of the worst flooding we’ve seen since Sandy.

We are monitoring conditions closely and coordinating with local, state, and federal officials.

Please stay off flooded roads, follow emergency alerts, and take this storm https://t.co/Nm2dlcWpLy

🚨 The PROOF Act just passed the House.

206 Democrats voted against fighting fraud.

Making sure taxpayer dollars go to the people who actually need them should not be controversial. https://t.co/TYIeTCl9ZF

This should be pretty simple.

If taxpayer money is being stolen, the Justice Department should be able to get the records and go after the people stealing it.

States should not be able to stand in the way. https://t.co/ibAgifntQH

A baby boy, hit by an illegal driver with an unenforced removal order.

A little girl, taken from her bed and assaulted by a man who shouldn't have been here.

Yet New Jersey is spending $20.2 million on legal defense for illegal immigrants.

Whose side is this state on? https://t.co/QohQ7yOH9i

Elections can come down to one vote.

So when hundreds of noncitizens cast ballots in New Jersey, we asked a pretty simple question: how did this happen?

Instead of answers, the state has stonewalled us every step of the way. https://t.co/UMu5g350xL

The state of New Jersey knew for TWO YEARS that 6,600 noncitizens had been improperly registered to vote.

Two years is a long time to keep something like that quiet.

People have every right to ask why. https://t.co/fGsJ2A9x8n

States should not be able to obstruct fraud investigations involving federal taxpayer dollars.

But that is exactly what is happening right now. 

Four states refused TWICE to provide requested SNAP data, forcing DOJ to sue just to get it.

I introduced the PROOF Act to give the

To all who are celebrating Rosh Hashanah, Leshana tovah!

Wishing everyone a happy and sweet new year.

There is a time and place for everything. 

The 9/11 Memorial is not it.

Show some respect. https://t.co/pO0p9Jibog

Twenty-five years ago marks the day our world changed forever.

We remember every life lost, every family changed forever, and every first responder who chose to run toward danger.

We will never forget. https://t.co/p0UszrKNRg

A 6-year-old girl was kidnapped from her home and sexually assaulted by an illegal immigrant in New Jersey.

He had already been in ICE custody in 2024 and was RELEASED back into our communities.

She deserved to be protected.
https://t.co/ANgWBkf5SY

One year ago, Charlie Kirk was assassinated for standing up for what he believed.

He changed conservative politics in this country and inspired a generation of young Americans to get involved and speak up.

What he built will endure. https://t.co/m0q6Ajrzio

Happy Labor Day!

South Jersey is proudly built by people who know the value of a hard day’s work.

Hope everyone enjoys a well-earned day with family and friends.

Burlington Stores was founded right here in New Jersey.

Now they’re joining a growing list of businesses fleeing the state.

Can you blame them?

Years of sky-high taxes and anti-business policies are driving jobs and opportunity out of New Jersey. https://t.co/RnrYYyNhie

We knew something was wrong with South Jersey’s electric bills.

We kept pushing, we asked FERC to audit Atlantic City Electric, and now we know we were right.

South Jersey families were being overcharged, and they deserve their money back.
https://t.co/q4IcaKuDgf

"Unlicensed Trenton woman" = an illegal immigrant from Guatemala with an active ICE detainer.

Tell the whole story. https://t.co/jrYXHODlCH

Democrats are sick of our hearings on the consequences of sanctuary policies.

We're sick of burying innocent Americans killed by the criminal illegal immigrants those policies protected.

We'll stop when the funerals do. https://t.co/w8RVcbGtGx

A baby is dead because of the reckless actions of two illegal aliens who never should have been in this country to begin with.

New Jersey needs to do the right thing and turn them over to ICE.

No more sanctuary. https://t.co/JVKVV0fBJa

Five years ago today, 13 American heroes were killed at Abbey Gate because of a disastrous withdrawal that never should have ended the way it did.

We owe those heroes a promise that America will never forget what happened that day. 🇺🇸 https://t.co/VZjbt2VbEk

We wrote the Governor to ask a simple question: how were thousands of noncitizens able to register to vote in New Jersey?

She answered with 3 pages of political talking points and personal smears — and no answers.

It was beneath her office. We will not stop pursuing the facts.

Today is the deadline, and we still don’t have an adequate response from the Governor.

I said from the start: this isn’t going away.

We will not stop pursuing until we get the full truth.

We will protect every American vote and make sure this never happens again. https://t.co/bUyDMxDhPR

American elections should be decided by American citizens.

That’s not radical. That’s common sense.

Pass the SAVE America Act. https://t.co/GHNj9ehERV

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
